what: One residue, several choices, or any residue
title: Glyco-regex syntax, step by step
text: Start residue name, family, choice: vertical bar | means “.” Square brackets collect alternatives. negated alternative (inside [^...]) must describe one residue, multi-residue path. dot mean “number residues.” Residue modifications matter. example, Gal6S asks sulfated Gal, whereas plain Gal match modified residue: Use residue names supported glyrepr. slash can also express residue choices, Gal/Man; [Gal|Man] makes alternatives explicit.
code: residues <- c("Gal", "GalNAc", "Man", "Fuc") data.frame(   residue = residues,   gal = rex_detect(residues, "Gal"),   hex = rex_detect(residues, "Hex"),   gal_or_man = rex_detect(residues, "[Gal|Man]"),   not_fuc = rex_detect(residues, "[^Fuc]") ) #>   residue   gal   hex gal_or_man not_fuc #> 1     Gal  TRUE  TRUE       TRUE    TRUE #> 2  GalNAc FALSE FALSE      FALSE    TRUE #> 3     Man FALSE  TRUE       TRUE    TRUE #> 4     Fuc FALSE FALSE      FALSE   FALSE rex_detect("Gal6S(b1-4)GlcNAc", c("Gal6S", "Gal", ".")) #> [1]  TRUE FALSE  TRUE

Finding Gal-GlcNAc therefore establish Gal terminal GlcNAc branches. Alternatives can describe whole paths : choice belongs inside square brackets. bare Gal|Man supported.

title: Get Started with glyrex
text: Sometimes want include one sugar. Write alternatives inside square brackets, separated |, can read “”: asks whether structure contains Gal Man. glyrex also provides familiar sugar families: Hex includes Gal, Glc, Man; HexNAc includes GlcNAc GalNAc; Sia includes Neu5Ac, Neu5Gc, Kdn. finds two sialylated examples without requiring particular member sialic acid family linkage. Two choices useful comfortable basics: [^Fuc] mean “fucose branch.” fucosylated LacNAc still matches [^Fuc]-GlcNAc, Gal Fuc. Use (!Fuc-) want branch absent. Also notice ^ different meanings inside [^Fuc] start ^Gal.
code: rex_detect(glycans, "[Gal|Man]") #>      lacnac  sialylated fucosylated        both     mannose  #>        TRUE        TRUE        TRUE        TRUE        TRUE rex_detect(glycans, "Sia-Galb4-GlcNAc") #>      lacnac  sialylated fucosylated        both     mannose  #>       FALSE        TRUE       FALSE        TRUE       FALSE

Results use standardized IUPAC representation, written form may differ input. extracted fragment can retain linkage information attached rest glycan. ending GlcNAc(b1- retains β anomer donor position 1 fragment’s reducing end; indicate extra residue failed search. rex_extract() returns one match per structure. retrieve matches, use rex_extract_all(): results collected separately input glycan. two Man residues separate matches even though kind sugar. complex patterns, matches can overlap. Match identity includes matched residues residues assigned named capture, different sites remain distinct even extracted strings equal. first consumed residue capture assignments, first successful trace takes precedence later nested traces; incomparable branch choices survive. Strict subsets removed capture assignments agree. Greedy/lazy repetition controls search preference, different captured repeat lengths retained. Larger matches come first, followed minimum residue ID deterministic node/capture tie breakers. Thus “first” mean leftmost piece written input, counts necessarily counts independent, non-overlapping motifs. See ?rex_detect details.

title: Regular Expressions for Glycan Structures
text: glymotif provides concise syntax matching glycan motifs. However, exact motif matching may sufficient express complex structural constraints. example, sialyl-LacNAc motif without fucosylation specified using bare IUPAC-condensed sequence. address limitation, glyrex introduces dedicated glyco-regex syntax enables flexible expressive pattern matching.

title: Regular Expressions for Glycan Structures
code: library(glyrex) x <- c(   "Gal(b1-4)[Fuc(a1-3)]GlcNAc(a1-",   "Gal(b1-4)GlcNAc(b1-",   NA_character_ ) p <- rex_compile("Galb4-(Fuca3-)GlcNAc") rex_detect(x, p) #> [1]  TRUE FALSE    NA rex_extract(x, p) #> [1] "Fuc(a1-3)[Gal(b1-4)]GlcNAc(a1-" NA #> [3] NA rex_match(x, "(?<antenna>Galb4)-GlcNAc") #>      match                 antenna #> [1,] "Gal(b1-4)GlcNAc(a1-" "Gal(b1-" #> [2,] "Gal(b1-4)GlcNAc(b1-" "Gal(b1-" #> [3,] NA                    NA rex_locate_all(x, p) #> [[1]] #>     nodes edges #> 1 1, 2, 3  1, 2 #> #> [[2]] #> [1] nodes edges #> <0 rows> (or 0-length row.names) #> #> [[3]] #>   nodes edges #> 1    NA    NA

title: glyrex 0.1.0
text: Initial release. Get Started glyco-regex syntax vignettes introduce structural queries biological examples. New rex_compile() validates compiles reusable glycan patterns residue classes, linkage constraints, branches, repetition, anchors, lookaround, named captures. New rex_count() rex_detect() count detect structural matches. Query functions accept glycan strings format supported glyparse::auto_parse(), including mixed-format vectors, well glyrepr_structure vectors glyrepr-compatible igraph objects. New rex_extract() rex_extract_all() return matching glycan fragments preserving reducing-end anomeric information. New rex_locate() rex_locate_all() identify nodes edges structural matches. New rex_match() rex_match_all() return structural matches named captures. New rex_subset() rex_which() select matching glycans indices.
